# autoseed (Go)

> Reads a GORM or ent model — schema.Parse for GORM, entc.LoadGraph for ent — derives foreign-key
> insertion order (stable topological sort), resolves cycles (a nullable edge in two passes, a
> required-only cycle by naming it), and writes referentially valid rows through gormseed.Seed or
> entseed.Seed — real inserts, tested against real PostgreSQL and MySQL. Status: in development;
> gormseed.SeedCoverage and locale are still design, not code. Read "Implemented today" vs
> "Planned" below before generating code.

Unlike every other Go seeder, nothing is declared by hand — no YAML fixtures, no hand-written
Seed() loops, no files numbered 01_, 02_ to get foreign-key order right. The model is the
specification.

Sibling project: EFCore.AutoSeed (same author, same design, .NET).

- Module: `github.com/danellalc/autoseed`
- Adapters: `autoseed/gormseed` (GORM, implemented), `autoseed/entseed` (ent, implemented)
- Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL tested against real containers by the property/integration suite; SQLite
  runs `Seed`/`Explain` in the package's own Example tests and the runnable example, not yet the same
  property/orphan-check suite
- License: MIT
- Status: in development

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/danellalc/autoseed
```

## Implemented today

```go
import (
    "github.com/danellalc/autoseed"
    "github.com/danellalc/autoseed/gormseed"
)

models := []any{&Customer{}, &Order{}, &OrderItem{}}

// Writes referentially valid rows, in dependency order. 1,000 Customer rows;
// Order and OrderItem scale from a long-tail draw per parent row.
err := gormseed.Seed(ctx, db, models, autoseed.WithSeed(42), autoseed.WithScale(1_000))

// Reads the model, derives insertion order, resolves cycles. Writes nothing.
plan, err := gormseed.Explain(db, models)
fmt.Println(plan.Report())
```

`models` is the exhaustive set of GORM structs to include: a `*gorm.DB` keeps no registry of every
struct it has ever used, unlike an EF Core `DbContext`, so the list is stated explicitly on every
call. `Explain`'s `db` may be `nil`, or not yet connected to a real database — reading a model is
pure reflection; `Seed` needs a real, migrated connection since it writes.

```go
import (
    "github.com/danellalc/autoseed"
    "github.com/danellalc/autoseed/entseed"
)

// schemaPath is the Go import path (or relative path) to the package
// holding the ent.Schema definitions, typically "./ent/schema" — ent
// exposes its resolved schema graph only through entc.LoadGraph, which
// loads it from source, so there is no model list to pass explicitly
// the way gormseed needs one.
err := entseed.Seed(ctx, client, "./ent/schema", autoseed.WithSeed(42), autoseed.WithScale(1_000))

plan, err := entseed.Explain("./ent/schema")
fmt.Println(plan.Report())
```

`entseed`'s `client` is the generated `*ent.Client` (or a type embedding one); it must not be nil.
ent has no composite primary keys, so a composite-key "attributed join" or ternary/N-ary
relationship is expressed there as a surrogate ID plus a composite `UniqueConstraints` entry
(`index.Fields(...)`/`index.Edges(...)` in the ent schema), not a composite primary key — both
adapters' cardinality capping understands either shape. A many-to-many edge (ent has no
addressable join-table entity for one, unlike GORM's auto-generated join struct) is read but not
generated: it appears once, by name, in `Explain`'s Skipped section.

`autoseed/inference` (~16 value-generation rules, gofakeit-backed) is what `Seed` calls per field:
Email/Name/Phone/URL/Street/City, coherent CreatedAt/UpdatedAt and Price×Quantity=Total, a
soft-delete field left nil (not deleted) 90% of the time and, for the rest, a timestamp no
earlier than the row's own CreatedAt/UpdatedAt, generic fallbacks by Go type, and one rule with
no opt-in — any string field named `Cpf` or `Cnpj` (case-insensitive suffix, any project)
generates a Brazilian document number with a valid check digit. This is not locale-gated —
there is no locale mechanism yet — so a non-Brazilian project with a coincidentally matching
field name gets Brazilian-format data. Every rule's string output, named or generic, is
truncated to the column's declared size, by rune not by byte, before it reaches the database. A
field typed `sql.NullString`/`NullInt64`/`NullBool`/`NullFloat64`/`NullTime` (and the narrower
`NullInt32`/`NullInt16`/`NullByte`), or a Go pointer field, is matched against rules by its
wrapped/pointed-to type, so `Email sql.NullString` still gets EmailRule's treatment.
`autoseed.WithNilRate(rate)` sets the per-row probability such a field is left out entirely
instead, producing a real database NULL — 0 by default, so every existing call keeps its current
behavior unless a project opts in.

## Planned, not implemented yet

These identifiers do not exist in the module. Do not generate calls to them.

```go
err := gormseed.SeedCoverage(db, models)
opts := autoseed.WithLocale("pt_BR")
```

Coherence across DIFFERENT entities (a child row's CreatedAt at or after its parent's) is not
built either; coherence today is same-row only.

## Guarantees

- Every foreign key `Seed` writes references a row that was actually inserted — verified against
  real, containerized PostgreSQL by a property-testing suite (random seed and scale), not asserted
  from reasoning alone. MySQL and SQLite get a narrower, non-property test surface today.
- Same seed, same data, across runs and machines. Map iteration never affects output.
- A required foreign key cycle returns `autoseed.ErrUnsatisfiableCycle` naming the real cycle —
  every independent unsatisfiable cycle in one model, not just the first found — rather than a
  database throwing a constraint violation. A nullable one is inserted null, then patched in a
  second pass once every row exists; breaking a cycle defers only the one nullable edge actually
  needed, never every nullable edge in it.
- A duplicate value for a field tagged `unique` (single-column, string only) is rewritten with a
  random numeric suffix, retried up to 20 times, before `ErrUnsatisfiableUniqueness` names it. A
  composite unique constraint (GORM's `uniqueIndex` tag; ent's `index.Fields`/`index.Edges`) with
  at least one non-foreign-key string column gets the same treatment on its tuple; two constraints
  that share a rewritable field are resolved together, not independently, so fixing one can never
  silently reopen a duplicate under the other. A constraint spanning only foreign key columns is
  left to the generation plan's cardinality cap instead, described below.
- A field GORM recognizes as its soft-delete column (`gorm.DeletedAt`) is left unset (visible) on
  about 90% of rows and given a past timestamp (deleted) on the rest — a fixed rate, not yet
  configurable.
- `autoseed.WithNilRate(rate)` leaves a Nullable field's value out entirely at that per-row
  probability, producing a real database NULL — a field is only Nullable when its Go
  representation can actually hold one (a pointer, a `database/sql` wrapper, or, for ent, any
  `Optional()` field, which its own `ClearField` handles uniformly). A plain, non-pointer field a
  schema happens to allow NULL at the column level, but with no Go-level way to represent absence,
  is never subject to this — generating nothing meaningful for it would just be a Go zero value
  wearing a NULL's name.
- A composite key — the entity's own primary key, or a `UniqueConstraints` entry spanning foreign
  key columns — covered by a driver reference plus one OR MORE other required references (a
  many-to-many join table, an "attributed join" entity with extra columns, or a ternary/N-ary
  relationship with three or more participants) never generates more children for one driver row
  than the other participants can jointly supply distinct combinations for — capped at the product
  of their own row counts. A shared-primary-key one-to-one (the GORM equivalent of EF Core's table
  splitting) never generates more than one child per driver row. A self-referencing participant
  (both foreign keys targeting the same entity, e.g. a "follows" table, or a participant
  referencing its own driver's target) is recognized the same way — participants are told apart by
  their own foreign key columns, never by target name — and never generates a row that pairs with
  itself. Any of these, uncapped, would risk colliding on the same key.
- Embedded structs are written as columns, never as their own table.
- Unsupported constructs (GORM's polymorphic associations; ent's many-to-many edges, for now) are
  skipped BY NAME in the Explain report, never silently misread or misgenerated.
- A Go named-integer "enum" (`type Status int` with `iota` constants) is generated as a plain number
  in the generic fallback's range, not restricted to a declared constant — Go's reflection cannot
  enumerate a type's declared constants the way C#'s `Enum.GetValues` can, so this is a language
  limit, not an unported rule.
- A primary key field is assumed database-generated only when it's also auto-increment. Any other
  primary key field — a natural key on a standalone entity (e.g. an app-generated UUID), or the
  one column of a composite key not covered by any reference (an `EffectiveDate` alongside
  `WarehouseID`+`ProductID`) — is generated like any other field now, using whatever rule matches
  its Go type. A type no rule recognizes (a custom `driver.Valuer` a database/sql nullable
  wrapper isn't one of) fails named with `ErrUnsupportedField` instead of being silently left at
  its zero value.
- `Seed`'s `ctx` is honored by the real database calls (batch inserts, the deferred-cycle
  transaction), not just in-memory value generation — a canceled or deadline-exceeded context
  stops in-flight writes. `Seed(ctx, nil, ...)` returns `gormseed.ErrNilDB` rather than panicking.
  `autoseed.PlanGeneration` and `autoseed.EnsureUnique` return `ErrNilSeed` for a nil
  `*SeededSource`, and `PlanGeneration` returns `ErrInvalidScale` for a negative
  `Options.Scale`, rather than panicking.

## Common mistakes when using this library

- Do not generate a call to `gormseed.SeedCoverage` — it does not exist yet. Use `gormseed.Seed`
  with a small `WithScale` for a small dataset instead.
- Do not omit a related model from `models` — `Seed`/`Explain` return `ErrUnknownReference` naming
  what's missing, rather than a partial or guessed result.
- Do not order entities manually. Order is derived from the model's foreign keys.
- Do not pass a nil or unmigrated `db` to `Seed` — unlike `Explain`, it writes, and needs the
  tables to already exist. A nil `db` returns `gormseed.ErrNilDB`; an unmigrated one returns
  whatever error the database driver gives for a missing table. `entseed.Seed`'s nil client check
  returns `entseed.ErrNilClient` the same way.
- Polymorphic associations (GORM) and many-to-many edges (ent) are read but not generated; they
  appear as skipped in the Explain report, never as a reference.

## Not supported

- ORMs other than GORM and ent (others on demand with traction).
- Databases other than PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite.
- Production data anonymisation. No cloud, no service.
